acceptance: An agent that reads only `AGENTS.md` and the pages it links can find the post-merge step and the exact command, including where `EXPECTED_HEAD_OID` comes from.
Following that step on a freshly squash-merged pull request removes the worktree and the local branch, shown once with the commands and output recorded on this item.
The decision on a `worktree-remove` hint is recorded; if added, a test shows it prints for a merged branch and not for an unmerged one, and deletes nothing extra.
`make agent-instructions-check` passes with the added text.
context: Decisions 2026-11-13: the step is documented on a page `AGENTS.md` already links (`docs/agent/merge-authority.md`), not in `AGENTS.md`; `make worktree-remove` gets no hint and deletes exactly what it does today. Delivered as a member of registered batch `member-rule-docs`.
description:
After PR #4170 merged on 2026-11-12 the session removed its worktree with `make worktree-remove`, which runs `git worktree remove` and keeps the local branch (`remove_worktree` in `scripts/worktree_lifecycle.sh`). `docs/batch-member-subagent-rule` is still in the primary clone. The targets that also retire the branch exist (`make worktree-finish WORKTREE_PATH= EXPECTED_HEAD_OID= [APPLY=1]`, `make worktree-reap`, `make branch-prune-merged`) but are named only in `make help`: neither `AGENTS.md` nor any file under `docs/agent/` mentions them, and the write close-out rule ends at the merged pull request without a step for the worktree. On 2026-11-13 the primary clone held 219 local branches, of which `git branch --merged origin/develop` lists 6; squash merges hide the rest from that test.

Related, not duplicates: agent-leftover-branches-and-clone-drift-20261109 (a one-off cleanup of named branches) and branch-prune-merged-exhausts-github-quota-20261112 (a defect in the prune target).

Decision gates.
- Decide where the step lives: one clause in the close-out rule in `AGENTS.md`, or a `docs/agent/` page it already links. `AGENTS.md` is near its size budget (agent-instruction-budget-headroom), so prefer the linked page unless the owner wants it in the guide.
- Decide whether `make worktree-remove` should print a hint naming `worktree-finish` when the branch's pull request has merged, or stay silent. Do not change what it deletes without an owner decision.
- Bulk removal of the existing backlog is a separate, destructive action: it needs the owner's approval in the task that does it, and is not part of this item.

Guardrails.
- No branch or worktree is deleted under this item except the author's own throwaway test branch.
- The documented step must use the evidence-checked target (`worktree-finish`), never `git branch -D` by hand, and must keep the dry-run default.
- Agents still never run `git worktree prune` or `gc`.
